category: inference endpoint, volunteer GPU network, anonymous key

per_object_cap.stated: not applicable: an inference endpoint stores nothing for the caller

egress.terms: the response is the payload; no separate egress term is published

reliability_note: anonymous requests are the first restricted under high load, and a job not served within the time limit times out

free_tier.stated: Text generation on volunteer GPUs with no account: the README gives API key 0000000000 for anonymous use and 'No need to register'. Anonymous requests have the lowest priority and the service 'may be restricted for anonymous users during high load'. Kudos never expire.

tooling: REST/curl POST with apikey: 0000000000 for anonymous use; Python horde-sdk or any HTTP client; base URL https://aihorde.net/api
chaining: text jobs are served by whichever volunteer worker hosts the requested model, so the per-model queue ETA, not a quota, decides latency

limits.value: no per-key quota is published for anonymous use; anonymous requests have the lowest priority and a request that finds no resources within the time limit times out. At the read: 97 text requests queued, 30 text workers on 64 text threads, 27861 tokens generated in the past minute
per-model queue ETA across the 28 listed text models ran from 0 seconds to 516 seconds

2 submits a second and 90 a minute from one address, 2 submits a second for one personal key, and 60 status reads a minute for one request from one address; Retry after the Retry-After header. Anonymous clients share one limit on concurrent requests and can get 429 TooManyPrompts.

binding_note: the queue binds: anonymous jobs wait behind jobs from accounts holding kudos, and a job not served within the time limit times out

identity_cost.detail: the API key 0000000000 needs no registration; a registered account (OAuth2 login or a pseudonymous key) gets higher priority

confidence_note: Route, method, request shape and anonymous key are quoted from first-party pages read 2026-11-18; the OpenAPI spec was captured. A dry-run POST answered HTTP 200 and a real submit with the anonymous key answered HTTP 202 and reached done true with a state ok generation, so an anonymous completion is measured. The pool figures in limits[] remain point-in-time listings read once.

submit route, poll route and where the generated text is read
evidence.quote: The client submits it with `POST /v2/generate/text/async`, polls `GET /v2/generate/text/status/<id>` until `done` is true, and reads the text from `generations`.

evidence.proved: the first-party OpenAPI spec defines the POST operation at /v2/generate/text/async; no synchronous /generate/text path is defined
evidence.quote: Initiate an Asynchronous request to generate text

evidence.proved: the apikey header is required and the anonymous key is 0000000000
evidence.quote: | `apikey` | Your API key, or `0000000000` for anonymous use. The header is required, so an anonymous client sends the anonymous key explicitly. |

notes: Image generation on the same network is a separate offer (compute/ai-horde). The text catalogue changes with whichever volunteers are online. The HTTP 405 recorded against https://aihorde.net/api/ is a wrong-method response from the API docs root; the text completion route is POST https://aihorde.net/api/v2/generate/text/async. An anonymous completion was obtained on 2026-11-18 with the public key 0000000000.
interface_detail: REST async text generation; POST a JSON body with prompt and params to https://aihorde.net/api/v2/generate/text/async with an apikey header (0000000000 for anonymous), then GET https://aihorde.net/api/v2/generate/text/status/<id> to read generations[].text; DELETE the same status path cancels; an OpenAI-compatible chat front is also served at https://oai.aihorde.net/v1
